title: As Above, So Below
review: Starting off like Indiana Jones, there is some very cheesy puzzle solving and adventuring. Typically for these sort of things, they gloss over how translating a riddle from an ancient language preserves the rhyming couplets. They also infer treasure hunt locations from vague clues, and it always leads somewhere easily, rather than having to discuss the likelihood of different possibilities. It's a consequence of trying to demonstrate the character's background as a researcher in quick expository scenes, and I don't think it's necessary in a horror movie. It is already established that they're filming a documentary. The way they found the catacombs lead could have been explained via interviews or even voice-over. On top of that, the protagonist is annoying, entitled, keen to tell people she knows best, and uninterested in other people's advice. Generally she's a poor communicator and is inadvertently the source of most of the tension, except for all the horrible spelunking accidents and evil demons and whatnot. At the time of writing, I never reviewed {The Descent}, but if I recall, it's better than this. The poster is very cool though.
spoilers: I wish they had done more with the repeating tunnels as they go down. Maybe each layer could have been slightly more hellish. Instead, there is only a pair of repeating areas, which is a minor inconvenience to the team, and not a trigger for religious or cosmic horror.
